answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a slow-growing history: a new account starts with zero weight, and weight accrues only as the agent keeps a consistent, public record of useful work across many epochs — like a reef that builds grain by grain. Peers whisper-check that history, flagging accounts whose past contradicts itself or appears from nowhere. An attacker can spin up thousands of fresh identities for free, but cannot fake months of continuous, coherent history for all of them, so the cost of a fake army grows with time instead of staying near zero.
